existing_roles.title: VP Manufacturing & Operations
existing_roles.description:
**Company Overview:**

ChocXO Chocolatier LLC is a leading North American premium chocolate manufacturer grounded in innovation, quality, and sustainability. We are a fast-growing, vertically integrated food manufacturing company operating across branded CPG and contract manufacturing. In the past year, we have scaled from one manufacturing facility to two, expanded our brand portfolio, and invested heavily in new capacity, innovation, and infrastructure.

**Our footprint includes Delta, British Columbia:**

Our 60,000 sq ft, fully automated, SQF Level 3 operational flagship, and Rockwall, Texas: Our new 225,000 sq ft manufacturing and warehouse complex, scheduled to open in 2027. We are now at the stage where systems, discipline, and repeatability matter as much as growth. We are building an enterprise-grade operations platform designed to scale—not a collection of plants dependent on heroics. We foster a culture of accountability where professionals thrive in structured environments and uphold rigorous standards.

**The Role:**  
The VP, Manufacturing & Operations reports directly to the President and leads plant operations at both of ChocXO’s manufacturing facilities: Delta, British Columbia and Rockwall, Texas. The Plant Managers at each location report directly to this role. The VP is the senior leader accountable for end-to-end operational performance across both sites, including manufacturing execution, food safety leadership, QA capability, OT systems oversight, and operational excellence.  
This is a hands-on, high-accountability leadership role. It requires deep manufacturing judgment, disciplined execution, and the confidence to stop production, reset standards, and enforce compliance when required.  
Key Responsibilities  
Multi-Plant Leadership

* Directly lead, develop, and hold accountable the Plant Managers for Delta, BC and Rockwall, TX
* Establish consistent expectations, KPIs, and operating cadence across all sites
* Ensure alignment between plant-level execution and enterprise standards
* Be visibly present in plants — especially during audits, trials, startups, and corrective actions

Operational Technology (OT) & Systems

* Provide leadership and oversight for OT systems supporting manufacturing operations
* Production monitoring
* Process controls
* Data integrity
* System discipline
* Ensure OT systems support repeatability, visibility, and accountability, not workarounds
* Partner with engineering and IT, but own operational effectiveness of systems on the floor

Food Safety, Quality & Audit Readiness

* Provide senior leadership on food safety expectations and audit readiness
* Set the standard for:
* Regulatory compliance
* Customer audits
* Third-party food safety certifications
* Build and lead a strong, credible QA organization
* Ensure quality systems are proactive, documented, and enforced — not reactive or cosmetic
* Personally set the tone that food safety and quality are non-negotiable

Process Discipline & Validation

* Establish and enforce standardized operating procedures (SOPs)
* Own process validation, trial approval, and GO / NO-GO decision gates
* Eliminate reliance on undocumented adjustments, heroics, or tribal knowledge
* Ensure processes run within defined parameters, with normal staffing, on repeat days

Inventory, Scrap & Loss Control

* Own accountability for scrap, rework, obsolete inventory, and yield loss
* Implement root-cause analysis and corrective action discipline
* Drive early-warning indicators and corrective action — not post-event explanations
* Embed cost awareness without compromising safety or quality

Training, Safety & Accountability Culture

* Build structured training systems for operators, supervisors, and plant leadership
* Lead facility safety as a core operational priority
* Establish and enforce an accountability culture:
* Clear expectations
* clear consequences
* Consistent follow-through
* Partner with HR, but retain operational authority and standards

Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

* Drive operational excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and morale
* Standardize best practices across plants
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives grounded in data and discipline
* Ensure improvements are institutionalized, not personality-dependent

AI, Automation & Digital Efficiency

* Use AI and advanced analytics to drive efficiency, throughput, and yield improvement across manufacturing and warehouse operations
* Identify, evaluate, and deploy practical AI tools (e.g., predictive maintenance, demand and production scheduling, quality and vision inspection, downtime and scrap analysis)
* Leverage AI-enabled insights from OT and ERP data to make faster, fact-based decisions and catch issues before they become losses
* Build team capability and comfort with AI tools, ensuring adoption is disciplined, documented, and compliant with food safety and data integrity requirements

What Success Looks Like

* Plant Managers are strong, accountable leaders — not firefighters
* Food safety audits are predictable, calm, and well-prepared
* QA is respected, not overridden
* OT systems provide clarity and control, not noise
* Scrap, rework, and operational “surprises” trend down materially
* Operations run consistently across plants and shifts
* The President is not required to intervene in day-to-day operations
* AI and automation tools are delivering measurable gains in efficiency, yield, and uptime

Required Experience & Profile  
Experience

* 15+ years in food manufacturing operations
* Proven multi-plant leadership experience
* Deep, practical expertise in:
* Food safety systems
* Quality assurance
* Audit management
* Allergen control
* Sanitation validation
* Process control
* Experience scaling operations in fast-growth environments
* Sufficient, hands-on experience applying AI, automation, and data analytics in a manufacturing environment to drive measurable efficiency gains
* Cross-border operations experience (U.S./Canada) strongly preferred

Leadership Attributes

* Exceptionally detail-oriented
* Disciplined, methodical, and structured
* Calm, firm, and decisive
* Comfortable holding leaders accountable
* Respected on the plant floor — not theatrical, not passive
* Strong presence without ego
* Comfortable saying “no” to bad ideas, shortcuts, or pressure

What We Are Not Looking For

* “Idea-first” operators without execution depth
* Leaders who normalize exceptions and workarounds
* Consultants masquerading as operators
* People who rely on heroics instead of systems
* Anyone uncomfortable enforcing standards or stopping production

Location & Travel

* Based at Rockwall, TX (DFW area). This is a fully on-site role, not remote, because presence matters
* Regular travel between the Rockwall and Delta plants is required, including during audits, trials, startups, and corrective actions
* Must be able to travel between the U.S. and Canada

Why This Role Matters  
This role is central to building a durable, scalable manufacturing platform.

**The right leader will:**

* Bring order to complexity
* Reduce operational risk
* Strengthen food safety and quality credibility
* Enable profitable, disciplined growth

If you are a serious food manufacturing operations leader who believes strong systems beat heroics, we want to talk.

This position provides strategic leadership to ensure the Division consistently delivers safe, reliable, compliant, and high-quality products and services that meet or exceed customer expectations while supporting the company’s growth, profitability, and operational objectives.

  

The role partners closely with Division leaders across Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Commercial, Finance, and Human Resources to establish a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, prevention, and customer excellence.

  

This position also serves as the subject matter expert for the enterprise-wide Permag Quality Management System and related regulatory and certification requirements, including ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485, ITAR, and other applicable customer, industry, and regulatory requirements. In this capacity this position supports and coordinates quality systems activities at sites across the entire Permag enterprise.

  

##### **Major Responsibilities - reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions:**

**Customer Quality & Strategic Relationships**

* Establish a customer-focused Quality culture throughout the Division.
* Provide leadership for significant customer quality issues, escalations, complaints, corrective actions, and recovery plans in the Division.
* Partner with Commercial and Operations leadership to protect and strengthen key customer relationships.
* Identify systemic customer quality trends and ensure corrective actions address root causes rather than symptoms.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Operational Quality & Continuous Improvement**

* Drive measurable improvements in first-pass yield, scrap, rework, nonconforming material, customer complaints, warranty/returns, CAPA effectiveness, and cost of poor quality.
* Establish Division Quality KPIs and performance expectations.
* Partner with Operations and Engineering to eliminate systemic process variation and improve manufacturing capability.
* Champion prevention-based Quality and continuous improvement methodologies throughout the Division
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Quality Organization & Talent**

* Establish organizational structure, roles, competencies, and succession plans necessary to support the Division’s current operations and future growth.
* Develop Quality leaders and technical talent through coaching, mentoring, and targeted development.
* Establish clear accountability and performance expectations across the Quality organization.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Risk Management**

* Identify and proactively manage Division Quality risks that could impact customers, operations, financial performance, reputation, or business continuity.
* Establish escalation protocols for significant Quality risks and provide leadership with timely visibility and recommendations.
* Partner with leadership to assess Quality risks associated with new customers, products, technologies, suppliers, facilities, and acquisitions.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**New Product & Business Growth**

Description:

**Lead Strategy. Drive Performance. Shape the Future.**

KSP Group, Inc/Jensen Metal Products is seeking a hands-on manufacturing leader to drive operational excellence, strengthen accountability, improve execution, and build scalable operating systems across our manufacturing businesses. This is not a corporate executive role designed to lead from a conference room.

We are looking for a proven change agent who is equally comfortable reviewing financial results, leading daily operational reviews, solving production challenges on the shop floor, and developing frontline leaders.

This is a multi-site position, initially focused on Jensen Metal Products and Jensen Powder Finishers. The successful candidate will build the structure, discipline, and performance culture needed to support long-term growth across KSP Group.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in fabrication and manufacturing environments, a strong operational and financial mindset, and a proven ability to lead teams through growth and transformation.

**About KSP Group**

KSP Group is a family-owned organization with a diverse portfolio of manufacturing and consumer product companies

* **Jensen Metal Products** – Custom metal fabrication, welding, machining, laser cutting, engineering and contract manufacturing solutions (Racine, WI)
* **Jensen Powder Finishers** – Advanced powder coating and finishing services (Sturtevant, WI)
* **Jensen Castings** – Manufacturer of premium GFRC concrete fire features (Richland Center, WI)
* **Real Flame** – A leading designer and manufacturer of fireplaces, fire tables, and outdoor living products sold through major retailers across North America (Union Grove, WI)

Together, our companies are built on innovation, craftsmanship, customer partnerships, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a visible impact, influence company strategy, and help shape the future of multiple growing businesses.

**What You'll Do**

Executive Strategic & Business Leadership

* Lead the development and execution of operational strategies that support long-term business objectives and growth initiatives
* Partner with executive leadership to establish priorities, allocate resources, and drive enterprise-wide operational improvements
* Lead plant leadership teams in defining strategic direction, performance goals, and key operational initiatives
* Identify opportunities for automation, process optimization, capacity expansion, and operational scalability

Financial & Operational Performance

* Own operational performance and P&L results across assigned manufacturing operations
* Develop departmental budgets, monitor spending, and ensure responsible management of operational resources
* Analyze manufacturing costs, labor efficiency, productivity metrics, and operating expenses to drive profitability
* Report on operational performance and improvement initiatives to executive leadership

Manufacturing Operations & Continuous Improvement

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives across fabrication, welding, machining, powder coating, assembly, engineering, and support functions
* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, 5S, root cause problem solving, and waste reduction efforts
* Improve throughput, quality, safety, delivery performance, and overall operational efficiency
* Lead cross-functional projects focused on sustainable operational gains and measurable business results

Leadership & Culture

* Build, coach, and develop high-performing operational leadership teams
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement
* Promote employee engagement while creating a safe, quality-focused work environment

Requirements:

**What We're Looking For**

* Demonstrated success leading directly from the manufacturing floor, including personal involvement in:
* Production planning and scheduling
* Labor performance management
* Quality improvement initiatives
* Corrective action processes
* Maintenance and equipment planning
* Capital investment justification
* Safety and operational accountability
* Frontline leadership development
* Proven track record of transforming entrepreneurial manufacturing organizations into process-driven, scalable operations through both strategic leadership and active engagement with frontline teams
* Ability to establish accountability without creating unnecessary bureaucracy
* Strong understanding of fabrication, welding, machining, finishing, assembly, materials management, and manufacturing cost drivers

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or related field, preferred
* Multi-site manufacturing leadership experience
* Lean Six Sigma certification
* Experience within both contract manufacturing and consumer products environments
* ERP/MRP system experience

**Travel Requirements**

* Regular travel between KSP Group facilities, including Jensen Metal Products, Jensen Powder Finishers, Jensen Castings, and Real Flame locations
* Frequent presence on manufacturing floors to support leadership teams, operational reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives
* Approximately 25-50% travel, primarily within Wisconsin and company operating locations
* Occasional overnight travel for customer visits, supplier meetings, strategic initiatives, and industry events

**About Us**

Jensen Metal Products is a metal fabrication business with over 100 years of experience serving the Midwest and surrounding regions with custom, quality sheet metal parts and assemblies. With a broad range of manufacturing capabilities, we produce a diverse portfolio of products, including our own line of fireplaces, which has been in production since 1970. We serve many types of businesses including the agricultural, retail, energy and healthcare fields. From engineering to packaging, our goal is to be a one-stop shop that exceeds our customers’ expectations for quality, delivery, great customer service and cost. At Jensen Metal Products we pride ourselves on having strong, long-lasting relationships with our employees and customers. We welcome you to join our team!

**Benefits**

* Competitive base salary plus profit sharing
* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with multiple plan options (HDHP and copay), FSA benefits, and the ability to use your existing HSA
* Company-funded medical deductible reimbursement — up to $1,000 (individual) / $2,000 (family)
* 401(k) with company match up to 4%
* Life and disability insurance and Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Paid time off and company holidays
* Annual Safety PPE Reimbursement
* A collaborative, team-oriented environment with direct access to leadership and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a growing organization
* Company-sponsored team events and outings that foster connection and celebrate team success

**Work Authorization**

Jensen Metal Products does not sponsor employment visas now or in the future. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future sponsorship.

**Recruiting Agencies**

Jensen Metal Products does not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing agencies, recruiting firms, or search agencies. Any unsolicited resumes submitted to Jensen Metal Products employees or through our application process will become the property of Jensen Metal Products, and no fee will be paid if the candidate is hired.

The Director of Contract Manufacturing understands key system constraints, quickly identifies critical process issues and successfully maintains key customer relationships. Has management responsibility for the strategy, relationship management, pricing and margin.

Description:

**Come Join the Toledo Tool & Die Team!**

Located close to the Michigan/Ohio border, Toledo Tool and Die has diligently served the people of both of those great states since 1940. It was a company founded on one simple principle: to do the finest work possible for our clients and to deliver on every promise we make. Today Toledo Tool & Die has four facilities in the Toledo area and one in Pioneer, Ohio.

Toledo Tool & Die is looking for a **Plant Manager** to join our team to support our continued growth.

This is a full-time position based in Toledo, Ohio. We offer competitive wages, growth opportunities, and a clean, safe work environment.

**WHAT TOLEDO TOOL & DIE CAN OFFER YOU:**

* Weekly pay
* 10 paid holidays
* 401k
* Full benefits

**WHAT MAKES YOU A GREAT FIT FOR THIS POSITION:**

* Previous experience at the plant manager level or equivalent
* Strong work ethic
* Positive attitude
* Consistent attendance
* Willingness to learn
* Safety minded

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, direction, and operational performance of an automotive manufacturing facility. This role ensures the plant meets or exceeds expectations for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and employee engagement while driving continuous improvement and operational excellence. The Plant Manager provides strategic leadership to all plant functions—including Production, Quality, Maintenance, Engineering, Materials, HR, and EHS—ensuring alignment with organizational goals and customer requirements. This position plays a critical role in developing a high-performing culture, optimizing manufacturing processes, growing talent, and ensuring the long-term success and competitiveness of the facility.

**ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:**

* Provide overall leadership and accountability for plant operations, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality production across robotic assembly, and related processes.
* Establish and execute plant strategies focused on safety performance, customer satisfaction, financial targets, operational efficiency, and workforce development.
* Lead, mentor, and develop department managers, supervisors, and cross-functional teams to drive a culture of ownership, continuous improvement, and high performance.
* Ensure compliance with safety policies, regulatory requirements, and environmental standards while actively promoting a world-class safety culture.
* Oversee adherence to IATF 16949, ISO, customer-specific requirements, and internal quality standards; partner with Quality to address issues and implement corrective actions.
* Monitor and manage plant KPIs including OEE, scrap, uptime, throughput, labor efficiency, and cost performance; ensure action plans are in place to address underperformance.
* Partner with Maintenance and Engineering to ensure equipment reliability, effective PM programs, and timely response to downtime or tooling issues.
* Oversee Materials/Logistics operations including inventory accuracy, material flow, scheduling, shipping, and customer delivery performance.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing initiatives, waste elimination efforts, standardized work implementation, and continuous improvement projects throughout the facility.
* Champion 5S, workplace organization, and visual factory standards across all production areas.
* Develop and manage annual plant budgets, capital expenditures, and long-term investment strategies.
* Collaborate with corporate leadership on production planning, capacity analysis, new program launches, engineering changes, and customer development initiatives.
* Ensure organizational compliance with HR, labor, ethics, and employment practices, including respect for human rights, non-discriminatory treatment, proper working hours, and wage law compliance.
* Build a positive employee relations environment through strong communication, coaching, and recognition; address workforce concerns and support effective engagement strategies.
* Lead regular plant meetings to ensure alignment, transparency, and effective communication across all levels of the organization.
* Represent the facility with customers, suppliers, auditors, and corporate partners.
* Employee is responsible for ensuring all environmental practices are in line with job scope / position. Examples include but not limited to: proper waste disposal practices, reporting of spills, non-compliance to permit, and addressing any improper practices.
* Employee is responsible for ensuring all human resources, ethics, and labor policies and practices are carried out in accordance with company policy and as in line with the scope of the position. Examples include but are not limited to: respecting the human rights of all workers (prohibition of forced labor, no child labor, maintaining appropriate working hours, and non-discriminatory treatment of all workers), abiding by ethical standards such as zero tolerance for bribery, corruption, extortion, and embezzlement, maintaining appropriate working hours of employees along with ensuring compensation is paid to workers that complies with all applicable wage laws.
* Assumes additional duties as assigned, which may fall outside the primary scope of the role.

**ISO / ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (EMS) RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Ensure that the resources needed for the environmental management system are available.
* Communicate the importance of effective environmental management and of conforming to the environmental management system requirements.
* Ensure that the environmental management system achieves its intended outcomes.
* Direct and support persons to contribute to the effectiveness of the environmental management system.

Requirements:

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business, Industrial Technology, or related field required; Master’s degree preferred.
* 10–15 years of progressive manufacturing experience with at least 5 years in a leadership role; automotive robotic assembly experience strongly preferred.
* Proven track record of managing large teams, complex manufacturing operations, and high-volume production environments.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, or similar continuous improvement methodologies.
* Strong understanding of automotive quality systems, including IATF 16949 and ISO standards.
* Demonstrated success improving plant performance, reducing costs, and driving operational excellence.

**GENERAL SKILLS/EXPERIENCE:**

* Strong leadership presence with the ability to inspire, influence, and motivate teams.
* Excellent communication skills for interacting with employees at all levels, customers, and executive leadership.
* Strong analytical, decision-making, and problem-solving abilities.
* Proven ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* High level of integrity, accountability, and professionalism.
* Ability to build a culture of trust, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

**SOFTWARE/COMPUTER SKILLS & EXPERIENCE:**

* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
* Experience with ERP or MES systems such as SAP, Oracle, Plex, QAD, or similar manufacturing platforms.
* Ability to interpret data dashboards, KPIs, and operational reports to guide decision-making.
* Demonstrated proficiency with digital tools used for production reporting, labor tracking, and quality management.

existing_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering
existing_roles.description:
Atomic Machines is building the Matter Compiler™, the first in a new class of AI-native, all-digital manufacturing systems that build working machines directly from code. The Matter Compiler (MC) is aimed at micro-machines: motors and gears the size of a grain of sand, robots small enough to work inside the body, cooling built directly into the chips that run AI, and the many devices like them that have been waiting on a way to build them. Its first product is PrimeSwitch™, an electromechanical power relay the size of a button battery that carries 150 amps continuous current and opens in 50 microseconds, about a thousand times faster than a conventional contactor. Founded by Jeff Holden — serial entrepreneur, ex-Amazon SVP and Uber's first Chief Product Officer — the company has raised $250 million to date.

Atomic Machines is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with offices in Emeryville and Santa Clara.

### **About The Role:**

We are seeking a Senior Manager, Platform Manufacturing Engineering to lead Production Manufacturing Engineering as we scale the Matter Compiler from pilot production into high-volume manufacturing. You will own the equipment that builds our devices — its build, integration, bring-up, qualification and reliability — and the team of engineers who deliver it.

**You are an engineer first.** This is a player-coach role and the player half is not decorative: you will spearhead the hardest projects on the critical path personally, in CAD and on the floor, and use that work as the vehicle for coaching everyone around you. The fastest way to set a standard here is to define it while you produce work that meets it, then mentor your team to achieve the same bar.

Mentoring here happens inside the work, not alongside it. You will pull engineers onto the projects you lead, hand off scope as they are ready for it, review their designs with real technical depth, and grow the next set of project leads out of people who learned by building with you.

The management half is real. You will hire against a plan rather than a wish list, develop engineers toward the next level, run performance honestly, and install the operating standards this function works to — documentation, change control, qualification and release discipline, and what "done" means before work leaves the group. You will plan the organization ahead of where the business is today, own headcount and capital budget, and get manufacturability and equipment requirements into specifications set by other teams rather than reviewing them at the end.

### **What You'll Do:**

* Spearhead the hardest equipment projects on the critical path yourself — architecture, CAD, build, bring-up and qualification — and bring engineers along on them as the primary way they develop.
* Lead a team of 5–10 engineers spanning equipment design, automation and controls, integration, and sustaining, through a mix of direct reports and technical leads.
* Set the engineering standard by producing work to it: reference designs, qualification plans, RCCAs and documentation your team can pattern from, with the reasoning made explicit so it transfers.
* Coach through the work — pair on designs, run technical reviews with real depth, hand off scope as engineers are ready for it, and grow the next set of project leads out of people who built alongside you.
* Own the delivery record for the function — the equipment, qualifications and production readiness your team commits to, against committed dates.
* Lead equipment deployment end to end: installation, validation, commissioning, acceptance testing, SOP/WI release and operator qualification.
* Run root cause and corrective action personally on the failures that matter, teach the method by doing it in front of the team, and drive the corrective actions across teams that do not report to you.
* Install and uphold the operating standards: documentation, change control, qualification and release discipline, RCCA method and closure, and how work is reviewed before it leaves the group.
* Plan organizational growth — forecast hiring needs ahead of demand, define roles and levels, build and defend the hiring plan, and manage headcount and capital budget with Supply Chain and Finance.
* Own and resolve escalated personnel situations arising from business and priority changes, rather than routing them away.
* Get manufacturability and equipment requirements into specification setting and design milestones with Design Engineering and Product, rather than reviewing at the end.
* Balance competing priorities with peer leaders so committed deliverables are still met, and own communication of impact and resolution path where they cannot be.
* Own contract manufacturer and automation supplier execution through final integration and test to conformant hardware on schedule.
* Drive throughput, yield, cost and uptime improvement — held with control limits, not delivered as one-time gains — and establish the operating metrics and reporting cadence leadership can rely on without chasing.
* Travel between Emeryville and Santa Clara sites as needed.

### **What You'll Need:**

* 7+ years of manufacturing or equipment engineering experience, including 3+ years managing engineers with 5 or more direct reports.
* **Current hands-on capability.** You still design in CAD, still debug hardware on the floor, and could take the hardest open task on your team's board tomorrow. We will test this directly in the loop.
* Proven ownership of automated production equipment end to end — architecture through mechanical, controls and software integration, into a qualified, released system running in production.
* Proficiency in CAD for equipment design (SolidWorks, Onshape, AutoCAD or similar), with recent personal use.
* A track record of **developing engineers through the work** — specific people who grew because you put them on projects you were leading, reviewed their designs, and handed off scope as they were ready for it.
* A track record of building out a functional group: defining roles, hiring against a plan, and installing the operating standards — not only inheriting an existing team.
* Experience leading a team spanning more than one discipline (e.g., equipment, controls/automation, integration, sustaining), including people whose work sits outside your own background.
* Ownership of headcount and capital budget, with resourcing tradeoff decisions made under real constraint.
* Depth across DFx, RCCA, eBOMmBOM conversion, qualification and acceptance testing, and PLM/document control and release (Arena a plus).
* Experience in semiconductor, solar, hardware-based biotech, EV, or similar high-tech industries.
* Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functionally without authority — specifically, getting manufacturing and equipment requirements into specifications owned by other teams.
* A first-principles mindset — you question assumptions, reframe problems from the ground up, and approach challenges with a foundational understanding rather than relying solely on precedent.
* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

### **Bonus Points For:**

* Experience standing up or rebuilding a manufacturing or equipment engineering function at a company moving from pilot to production scale.
* Experience staying technically current while managing — a design, patent, or build you personally delivered while running a team.
* Knowledge of basic coding: RSLogix, Ignition, Python, or C/C++.

Atomic Machines is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity and does not discriminate based on characteristics protected by applicable law. We are committed to an inclusive interview experience, including for individuals with disabilities. To request an accommodation, contact rc@atomicmachines.com. To help our recruiting team manage application volume and respond to candidates more efficiently, Atomic Machines may use AI-assisted tools.

existing_roles.description:
ElevateBio is a technology-driven company powering the industry forward by helping partners realize the potential of their therapies from design to commercialization. We have integrated a differentiated set of technologies, end-to-end services, and industry-leading manufacturing expertise to develop advanced therapies faster and more efficiently.

  

**The Role**

The Senior Director, Quality Control leads all Quality Control operations at ElevateBio's Waltham site, including QC Analytical Technologies (QCAT), QC Analytics, Testing Core, QC Microbiology, QC Raw Materials, and QC Logistics. The role is accountable for safe, compliant, inspection-ready, and predictable execution across a seven-day operating model, including product release and in-process testing, STAT support to Manufacturing, environmental and microbiological testing, raw material disposition, stability support, sample management, and analytical lifecycle enablement. The Senior Director establishes the QC operating strategy, capacity and resource plan, performance system, and leadership model required to meet manufacturing, client, and business commitments while sustaining laboratory excellence and data integrity.

**Here's What You'll Do**

**QC Strategy and Leadership**

* Lead the integrated QC organization, operating model, objectives, decision rights, talent strategy, and capability roadmap.
* Develop QC management and technical leaders while aligning headcount, seven-day coverage, facilities, equipment, systems, operating expense, and capital with demand.

**Predictable QC Operations and Laboratory Excellence**

* Own safe, compliant, and predictable execution of product release and in-process testing, environmental and microbiological monitoring, raw material disposition, stability, sample management, and client commitments.
* Ensure reliable seven-day operations through capacity planning, schedule control, tiered daily management, performance review, and timely escalation and recovery.
* Partner with Manufacturing to align readiness, prioritization, and rapid execution of STAT in-process samples within required decision windows.
* Drive laboratory excellence through standard work, right-first-time execution, efficient review and reporting, backlog control, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement.

**Analytical Technologies and Lifecycle Enablement**

* Provide leadership oversight for QCAT, including client technical interface, technology and method transfer, qualification and validation, method lifecycle management, equipment qualification, controls and critical reagents, and Digital QC.
* Ensure effective utilization of shared QC Resources, handoffs between QCAT and operational laboratories through clear readiness criteria, accountability, sustainable capacity, and post-implementation monitoring.

**Quality, Compliance, and Partnership**

* Ensure QC activities meet cGMP, approved procedures, specifications, quality agreements, data-integrity expectations, and regulatory commitments.
* Provide senior oversight of laboratory events, atypical or out-of-specification results, deviations, investigations, CAPAs, changes, risks, and inspection readiness.
* Represent QC in client governance, audits, regulatory inspections, release-readiness reviews, and escalations; communicate performance, constraints, risks, and recovery plans clearly.
* Serve as the senior QC partner to Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, Facilities & Engineering, MSAT, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, Digital, Process and Analytical Development, and site leadership.

**Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree in Biology, Microbiology, Biochemistry, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline; an advanced degree is preferred.
* At least 15 years of progressive experience in GMP Quality Control or analytical laboratory operations, including substantial leadership of managers and multi-functional teams.
* Demonstrated leadership of a broad QC organization supporting complex biopharmaceutical, biologics, cell therapy, gene therapy, or other regulated manufacturing operations.
* Strong knowledge of GMP laboratory controls, analytical testing, microbiology, environmental monitoring, raw materials, stability, sample management, analytical lifecycle activities, laboratory systems, data integrity, contract laboratory oversight, and quality systems.
* Demonstrated success improving schedule reliability, turnaround time, right-first-time performance, capacity utilization, investigation management, and inspection readiness.
* Experience leading seven-day operations and partnering with Manufacturing on time-critical in-process testing and operational decision windows.
* Experience supporting client audits, regulatory inspections, client governance, and significant quality or delivery escalations.
* Strong strategic planning, financial stewardship, organizational design, talent development, communication, decision-making, and stakeholder-management capabilities.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or demonstrated experience applying Lean Six Sigma, Lean Lab, and Digital Lab practices to improve laboratory flow, capacity, data visibility, and operational performance is preferred.
* Experience in a multi-program or CDMO environment is preferred.

**Physical and Environment Requirements:**

* Ability to stand, walk, bend and stretch for extended period of time
* Ability to lift 15-20 lbs
* Ability to push, pull, bend, kneel, twist and climb step ladders while wearing PPE.
* Ability to perform routine repetitive motions with use of arms, wrists and hands

**Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.**

We do it all while committing to integrity, sustainability, and giving back to our communities. Because doing so can fuel the very innovation we are pursuing.

**Job Summary**

The Senior Director, Semiconductor Sourcing and NPI Procurement leads the global strategy, sourcing, and supplier ecosystem for wafer foundry services, IP and EDA services, discrete actives semiconductors, and 3rd party NAND flash controller categories as well as the New Product Introduction Procurement function. This role is accountable for delivering cost competitiveness, supply assurance, and long-term resilience across a complex semiconductor value chain.

Partnering closely with engineering, manufacturing, and business leaders, the role drives category strategies, supplier performance, and risk mitigation at category and product level while enabling Micron’s growth and innovation priorities. Success in this role requires deep semiconductor domain expertise, strong commercial acumen, and the ability to lead large, global teams to deliver enterprise-level outcomes.

**Main Responsibilities**

* Define and execute global procurement strategies for wafer foundry services, IP and EDA services, discrete actives semiconductors, and 3rd party NAND flash controller categories to support business growth and operational excellence

existing_roles.title: Plant Manager III
existing_roles.description:
EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions helping industrial, infrastructure and defense customers address critical power and operational needs. The company delivers integrated solutions that combine energy storage technologies, power electronics, software-enabled intelligence, technical expertise and comprehensive global customer support. EnerSys supports customers across communications networks, data centers, energy infrastructure, material handling, transportation, aerospace and defense — including applications where power continuity is essential. Serving customers in more than 100 countries, EnerSys helps organizations manage energy more reliably, efficiently and intelligently in complex operating environments where uptime, safety and resilience matter.

  

**Job Purpose**
---------------

The Plant Manager will provide overall leadership for the phased development, start-up, ramp-up, and ongoing operation of the new lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility in Greenville, South Carolina. This is a unique opportunity to build a factory and its organization from the ground up in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment.

The role will evolve through multiple phases of the project, beginning with facility construction and operational readiness and progressing through equipment installation and commissioning, production launch, workforce ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale manufacturing operations.

The Plant Manager will be accountable for establishing the operating model, leadership capability, organizational structure, culture, management systems, and performance disciplines required to achieve excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and customer satisfaction.

This leader must bring broad manufacturing expertise in a high-volume, fully automated environment and understand the interdependencies across production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people. The successful candidate will combine strong operational and financial acumen with knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing and a demonstrated ability to build organizations, develop leaders, anticipate workforce needs, and establish strong relationships with employees, customers, suppliers, and business partners.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

**Factory Development, Start-Up & Operational Readiness**

* Provide operational leadership throughout the phased development of the Greenville facility, ensuring manufacturing and operational requirements are incorporated as the factory is constructed, commissioned, launched, and scaled.
* Partner with Engineering, Project Management, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, EHS, People & Culture, IT/OT, and other functions to establish comprehensive manufacturing readiness.
* Translate facility and project milestones into executable operational plans covering equipment, processes, workforce, training, materials, systems, safety, quality, and infrastructure.
* Ensure equipment, manufacturing processes, systems, organizational capability, and workforce readiness progress together so that potential gaps are identified and resolved before they impact production.
* Establish the operating systems, standard work, governance, performance metrics, escalation processes, and accountability required to transition successfully from project execution into manufacturing operations.
* Lead the operational transition through equipment installation and commissioning, qualification, production launch, ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale operations.

**Manufacturing & Operational Leadership**

* Provide end-to-end leadership of plant operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, capacity, employee performance, and overall manufacturing results.
* Maintain a comprehensive understanding of plant operating processes and ensure effective integration across production, maintenance, engineering, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, and supporting functions.
* Establish a culture of operational excellence, disciplined execution, accountability, continuous improvement, and structured problem solving.
* Establish and continuously evaluate plant KPIs to identify performance gaps, determine root causes, and drive sustainable corrective actions.
* Drive improvement in manufacturing productivity, equipment effectiveness, reliability, throughput, yield, quality, labor efficiency, and operating cost.
* Ensure appropriate manufacturing systems, controls, procedures, and escalation mechanisms are established as production volume and organizational complexity increase.
* Champion Lean manufacturing principles and create a culture in which continuous improvement is embedded throughout the organization.

**Lithium-Ion Cell Manufacturing**

* Provide leadership within a technically complex lithium-ion cell manufacturing environment.
* Apply practical knowledge of cell manufacturing processes, automated manufacturing equipment, process controls, materials, quality requirements, and production risks to operational decision-making.
* Work closely with Cell Engineering, Process Engineering, Quality, EHS, and other technical teams to establish safe, repeatable, high-quality manufacturing processes capable of operating at scale.
* Ensure plant teams understand the relationships among process capability, product quality, yield, throughput, equipment performance, manufacturing cost, and customer requirements.
* Support the effective introduction, industrialization, and scale-up of new manufacturing processes and technologies.

**Financial & Business Leadership**
-----------------------------------

* Own plant operating performance from both an operational and financial perspective.
* Develop and manage plant operating budgets, forecasts, labor plans, productivity targets, capital requirements, and cost-improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrate strong understanding of the economic drivers of manufacturing and translate operational performance into financial and business outcomes.
* Partner closely with Finance to understand and manage manufacturing cost, labor, productivity, inventory, scrap, yield, capital utilization, and other key plant performance drivers.
* Evaluate significant operational decisions through both manufacturing and financial lenses, balancing immediate execution requirements with the long-term capability and competitiveness of the plant.
* Establish strong cost-management and financial disciplines as the facility transitions from construction and start-up investment to sustainable manufacturing operations.

**Workforce Planning & Organizational Capability**

* Build the plant organization in phases aligned with facility construction, commissioning, production launch, ramp-up, and future operating requirements.
* Develop short- and long-term workforce plans to ensure the plant has the appropriate leadership, technical, skilled-trades, professional, and manufacturing capabilities required at each stage of growth.
* Anticipate talent, capacity, skill, and leadership gaps before they become constraints to manufacturing performance or future growth.
* Partner closely with People & Culture to develop recruiting, workforce planning, onboarding, training, retention, employee engagement, talent management, and organizational capability strategies.
* Establish clear organizational structures, decision rights, accountabilities, and leadership responsibilities as the facility grows and becomes operational.
* Develop workforce flexibility and organizational depth to mitigate single points of dependency and ensure business continuity.
* Regularly assess whether workforce capacity and capability are appropriately aligned with production requirements, operating plans, and future growth.

**Leadership Development & Succession**

* Recruit, build, coach, and develop a high-performing plant leadership team capable of successfully operating at increasing levels of scale and complexity.
* Establish a leadership culture where leaders are expected not only to deliver results but also to develop other leaders and build capability within their organizations.
* Partner with People & Culture to regularly assess leadership capability, organizational effectiveness, succession coverage, bench strength, and future talent requirements.
* Build strong succession pipelines for critical plant leadership and technical positions and ensure appropriate development plans are established for potential successors.
* Identify and develop high-potential talent through coaching, mentoring, expanded responsibilities, cross-functional experience, and targeted development opportunities.
* Establish sufficient leadership and technical depth to minimize organizational vulnerability and ensure continuity as the facility grows.
* Create a culture where talent development and succession planning are ongoing leadership responsibilities rather than periodic HR activities.

**Customer, Supplier & Stakeholder Leadership**
-----------------------------------------------

* Build strong, credible, long-term relationships with customers and ensure plant execution consistently supports quality, delivery, responsiveness, and customer commitments.
* Build strategic relationships with suppliers, equipment manufacturers, contractors, and other external partners critical to the construction, start-up, and ongoing operation of the plant.
* Work collaboratively with customers and suppliers to resolve issues quickly while protecting long-term business relationships.
* Serve as a senior representative of the Greenville operation with business leadership, customers, suppliers, community stakeholders, and other external partners as appropriate.
* Build strong cross-functional relationships across the broader organization and effectively navigate a complex, matrixed environment.
* Maintain a visible leadership presence throughout the plant and foster an employee environment built on communication, engagement, trust, accountability, and strong employee relations.

**Safety, Quality & Culture**

* Establish safety as a foundational operating principle and ensure appropriate systems, behaviors, and leadership accountability are embedded throughout the facility.
* Champion a quality-first mindset and ensure the organization consistently meets internal requirements and customer expectations.
* Build a high-performance culture characterized by accountability, collaboration, transparency, urgency, ownership, and continuous improvement.
* Establish clear expectations for leadership behavior and ensure those expectations cascade throughout the plant organization.
* Create an environment where employees understand how their work contributes to plant performance, customer success, and the broader business.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related discipline.
* Significant progressive leadership experience within complex, high-volume, highly automated, or advanced manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading a significant manufacturing operation with accountability across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and financial performance.
* Demonstrated experience supporting or leading the build and start-up of a new manufacturing facility, significant plant expansion, major manufacturing transformation, or complex production ramp-up.
* Strong knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing or relevant advanced manufacturing technologies and processes.
* Broad understanding of manufacturing operations and the interdependencies among production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people.
* Strong financial and commercial acumen with experience managing operating budgets, forecasts, manufacturing costs, capital investments, productivity, and business performance.
* Demonstrated success building, leading, coaching, and developing high-performing leadership teams.
* Experience with workforce planning, organizational design, talent development, and leadership succession.
* Demonstrated ability to build effective relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, executive leadership, and cross-functional partners.
* Proven ability to lead through ambiguity and rapidly changing priorities within a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
* Direct experience in lithium-ion cell manufacturing or large-scale battery manufacturing.
* Experience taking a newly constructed manufacturing facility through commissioning, production launch, volume ramp-up, and stabilized operations.
* Experience with highly automated manufacturing equipment and advanced manufacturing technologies.
* Strong working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, structured problem solving, operational excellence, and continuous-improvement methodologies.
* Experience working within a global manufacturing organization or complex matrixed business environment.

**General Job Requirements**
----------------------------

* This position requires working in a plant/warehouse environment. Therefore, expect varying working conditions.

protected_roles.description:
Job Description
  
  
Position Overview
  
  
Quality Lead, Director– QMS & Digital Quality Governance Analytical
  
Global Quality Management Systems
  
  
The Global Quality Group within our Company Manufacturing Division is seeking an experienced transformation lead in the capacity of Director– Quality Management Systems (QMS) & Digital Quality Governance, to provide strategic and operational leadership for the QMS workstream within a complex, enterprise-level laboratory transformation program.
  
  
This role is accountable for architecting, modernizing, and deploying a modernized, digitized Quality Management System tailored to support next-generation QC testing, end-to-end analytical digitization, instrumentation innovation, and laboratory automation.
  
  
The QMS Quality Lead will oversee the harmonization and evolution of quality processes—including deviation management, investigations, CAPA, change control, risk management (ICH Q9), and computerized systems validation (CSV/CSA)—to ensure seamless integration with modern automated laboratory workflows, LIMS, ELN, and digital data pipelines. In close partnership with the program leadership team, Site Quality heads, Analytical Development, Digital/IT Quality, and Regulatory Compliance, the incumbent will ensure that innovative operational models maintain rigorous compliance with global health authority regulations while driving efficiency, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.
  
  
Key Responsibilities and Requirements
  
The ideal candidate will combine deep technical expertise in global Quality Management Systems with a forward-thinking innovation mindset, translating digital and automated laboratory advancements into agile, compliant, and sustainable QMS frameworks.
  
  

* Strategic QMS Architecture & Modernization: Define, lead, and execute the QMS integration strategy for the lab transformation initiative, ensuring core quality processes (Change Control, OOS/OOE/OOT investigations, Deviations, CAPA, Method Transfer/Validation, and Batch Release support) are optimized, digitized, and natively integrated with automated laboratory systems
* Coding Experience: Experience and understanding on how coding translates to QMS and analytical functions. Responsible for overseeing the eQMS and ability to be able to review and understand the underlying code and how it is ensures compliance.
* Digital Quality & Data Integrity Governance: Partner with IT/Digital Quality and Automation engineers to embed robust Data Integrity by Design (ALCOA+) and Computer Software Assurance (CSA) principles into digitized laboratory platforms, instrument interfaces, and automated data flows.
* Regulatory Compliance & Inspection Readiness: Ensure all modernized QMS processes, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) comply with global cGMP regulations (FDA 21 CFR Part 11/210/211, EU Annex 11, ICH Q9/Q10, WHO). Drive inspection readiness strategies and author/review corresponding regulatory briefing documents and filing sections.
* Matrixed Program Leadership & Governance: Direct the QMS workstream governance forum, actively tracking milestone execution, interdependencies, risks, and critical paths. Provide regular data-driven progress updates, risk assessments, and escalation pathways to the Overall Quality Lead and executive steering bodies.
* Change Management & Operational Transition: Drive human-centered change management and training initiatives to support site-level and global QC laboratory adoption of digitized quality workflows, fostering a strong culture of quality and transformation agent mindset.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the central quality authority across laboratory operations, technology development, computerized systems validation, and regulatory affairs, eliminating silos and resolving complex compliance roadblocks.
* People Leadership & Oversight: Supervise and mentor quality specialists, compliance leads, and external consultants supporting QMS transformation, maintaining high standards of technical rigor, accountability, and development.

Required Experience
  
  

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmacy, Engineering, Life Sciences, or related discipline required; advanced degree (Master’s, PhD, PharmD, or MBA) strongly preferred.
* Experience: 10+ to 15+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical quality operations, quality systems, or compliance within a cGMP manufacturing and QC laboratory environment.
* Quality Systems Expertise: Proven track record in designing, optimizing, and overseeing enterprise-level QMS processes (Deviations, Investigations, CAPA, Change Control, Out of Specification, and Quality Risk Management) in laboratories subject to global health authority inspections (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA).
* Digital & Laboratory Systems Acumen: In-depth knowledge of laboratory digital ecosystems, including LIMS, ELN, CDS, SDMS, automated instrumentation, and their integration into enterprise QMS platforms (e.g., TrackWise, Veeva Vault QMS).
* Validation & Compliance Mastery: Strong understanding of Data Integrity expectations, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and modern risk-based validation methodologies (GAMP 5, Computer Software Assurance).
* Governance & Program Execution: Demonstrated success leading large-scale cross-functional workstreams, setting project milestones, proactively managing risk registers, and driving accountable execution.
* Communication & Influencing: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to present technical compliance strategies effectively to executive sponsors, auditors, and technical teams.

Preferred Experience
  
  

* Direct experience leading or supporting QMS transformation initiatives (e.g., transition from paper/hybrid to end-to-end digitized paperless QC environments).
* Working knowledge of automated testing platforms, robotics, or continuous manufacturing/testing control frameworks.
* Experience with global health authority inspections, pre-approval inspections (PAIs), and authoring QMS/Quality sections for regulatory dossiers (NDA, BLA, MAA).
* Practical application of Lean / Six Sigma methodologies to streamline quality workflows and cycle times.
* Programming experience is an asset, and or strong demonstrated ability to quickly learn.
* Experience supporting enterprise workforce strategy, technology evaluation, or transition initiatives.
* Experience managing external third party service providers, software vendors, and implementation partners in regulated environments.

**Required Skills:**  
Analytical Development, Cross-Functional Leadership, Digital Transformation, Enterprise Transformation, Executive Communications, GMP Compliance, Laboratory Quality Control, Project Governance, Quality Management Systems (QMS), Regulatory Strategies
  
  
**Preferred Skills:**  
Analytical Testing, Change Leadership, Program Governance

protected_roles.title: Director, Quality
protected_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

### **What you'll bring**

* 15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
* Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
* A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
* Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
* Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
* Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
* A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
* Preferred qualifications
* Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
* Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
* Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
* Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
* Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
* Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
* Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

### **Nice to have:**

* HW Experience
* Global distributor teams
* grown and org

### **Benefits**

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What we offer:

* Competitive salary and equity packages
* Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources
* An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family
* 20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off
* Paid sick leave and parental leave

Ōura takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. US locations are categorized into tiers based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future.

We are not considering candidates residing in the following states: Alaska (AK), Delaware (DE), Iowa (IA), Mississippi (MS), Nebraska (NE), South Dakota (SD), West Virginia (WV), and Wisconsin (WI).

ŌURA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Individuals seeking employment at ŌURA are considered without regard to age, ancestry, color, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, mental or physical disability, national origin, protected family care or medical leave status, race, religion (including beliefs and practices or the absence thereof), sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.

We will work to ensure individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.

Disclaimer: Beware of fake job offers!
  
We’ve been alerted to scammers posing as ŌURA recruiters, especially for remote roles. Please note:

* Our jobs are listed only on the ŌURA Careers page and trusted job boards.
* We will never ask for personal information like ID or payment for equipment upfront.
* Official offers are sent through Docusign after a verbal offer, not via text or email.

Stay cautious and protect your personal details.

Overview

:

**POSITION SUMMARY:** The Regional Director – Quality provides leadership for the assigned platforms’ clinical quality program. In partnership with physician leadership, the Regional Director – Quality supports clinical quality improvement, patient safety, clinician education, and quality governance. The Regional Director – Quality collaborates with facility partners, USAP’s data analytics team, and corporate leadership to advance quality initiatives and support physician-led clinical excellence.

Job Highlights

:

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**: (*The ideal candidate must be able to complete all physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation)*

  

* Leads the platform's clinical quality program in collaboration with physician leadership.
* Supports implementation of local and enterprise quality initiatives.
* Identifies opportunities to improve clinical quality and patient safety.
* Coordinates platform participation in enterprise quality initiatives, as applicable.
* Manages the case review process in collaboration with the local Clinical Quality Committee (CQC).
* Reviews unexpected clinical outcomes, referrals, trends, and other quality concerns.
* Conducts review of clinical events and recommends opportunities for system or practice improvement.
* Escalates issues through established governance pathways, as appropriate.
* Facilitates the development and implementation of quality improvement initiatives.
* Evaluates the effectiveness of quality improvement initiatives.
* Shares best practices across platforms.
* Develops and coordinates clinician education arising from quality initiatives, patient safety activities, case reviews, and other clinically relevant topics identified by the platform CQC.
* Orients new clinicians to the platform’s quality program.
* Supports the development, implementation, and ongoing review of clinical protocols and practice guidelines in collaboration with physician leadership.
* Reviews patient satisfaction feedback and trends to identify opportunities to improve clinical quality and patient safety.
* Partners with the data analytics team to define quality reporting needs, including relevant dashboards.
* Identifies data-informed opportunities for improvement in collaboration with the platform CQC.
* Supports the platform CQC.
* Partners with facility quality and physician leaders to advance quality initiatives, including representing the platform on facility quality committees, as appropriate.
* Coordinates quality reporting required by facility and payor contracts and applicable regulatory agencies.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

:

**K****NOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES** **(KSAs):**

  

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare or related field required, master’s degree preferred.
* 5+ years’ progressively responsible healthcare quality experience, preferably in a physician practice, ambulatory, or perioperative setting.
* Knowledge of quality improvement principles and patient safety.
* Knowledge of Power BI preferred.
* Knowledge of healthcare regulatory and accreditation requirements relevant to physician practice.
* Knowledge of clinical quality review methodologies and quality governance processes.
* Ability to interpret quality data and trends.
* Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.
* Ability to lead and facilitate committee discussions and communicate complex information to diverse audiences.
* Ability to build collaborative relationships with clinicians, facility leaders, and multidisciplinary teams.
* Experience leading quality improvement initiatives across multiple sites.
* Demonstrated ability to influence through collaboration and trust building.
* Demonstrated commitment to professionalism, integrity, confidentiality, and continuous improvement.
* Experience leading, mentoring, and developing a high-performing team.

* *The physical demands described here are representative of those that may need to be met by an employee to successfully p**er**form the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

* *Occasional Standing*
* *Occasional Walking*
* *Frequent Sitting*
* *Frequent hand, finger movement*
* *Use office equipment (in office or remote)*
* *Communicate verbally and in writing*

protected_roles.description:
**Your Opportunity as the Senior Manager Quality Assurance - Uncrustables**

This role is critical to ensure our Frozen Handheld & Spreads plants consistently meet our high standards for food safety and quality, as well as regulatory and customer requirements. You will lead quality assurance efforts across three sandwich manufacturing facilities and R&D pilot plant, balancing strategic oversight with hands-on project execution. Success in this role requires adaptability, attention to detail, and the ability to lead through influence.

**Location:** Orrville. OH Corporate

**Work Arrangements:**

* Hybrid – onsite a minimum of 9 days a month, primarily during core weeks as determined by the Company; maybe more as business need requires

* Flexibility to work outside of core hours, flow to the work, and travel to support plant / bakery issues as needed

* Travel – up to 35% annually

* Typically requires working 45+ hours per week, including on call

**In this role you will:**

* Provide leadership through being the primary liaison between Corporate QA and Uncrustables manufacturing facilities
